raw_case_text:
A 66-year-old Asian Indian male presented with a history of high-grade fever with chills and rigors, severe arthralgia, popular skin rash, and fatigue. He was diagnosed with Chikungunya fever based on IgM-positive results from his serum sample. Investigations revealed erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 34 mm at the end of 1 h, platelet counts of 150,000/mm3, hemoglobin of 13 g/dL, and total leukocyte count of 12,000/mm3. The patient received treatment elsewhere for the condition including supportive management by antipyretic agents, fluids, and supportive therapy. For arthritis, the patient was also advised oral hydroxychloroquine. Due to significant fluid loss and severe disease, the patient also developed acute renal failure requiring dialysis. Fifteen days after the onset of fever, the patient developed decreased vision and photophobia in both eyes. However, the visual symptoms were not further evaluated at this time given his systemic comorbidities.
Six weeks after the onset of fever, the patient presented to the Ophthalmology department for further evaluation of decreased vision, which remained persistent. Detailed examination revealed best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/60 in the right eye (OD) and 20/30 in the left eye (OS). No relative afferent pupillary defect was apparent. Slit-lamp examination showed the absence of inflammation in the anterior chamber. There was no evidence of vitritis at this time. Intraocular pressure was 12 mmHg in OD and 13 mmHg in OS. The dilated fundus examination of the OD showed the presence of peripapillary areas of depigmented healed retinitis lesions with retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) alterations. Similar lesions were seen near the inferior arcade and temporally. The macula was spared [Fig. 1]. The patient had the presence of a dense nuclear cataract in OD. Autofluorescence imaging (FAF) showed stippled irregular hypoautofluorescence in the nasal peripapillary lesions and hyperautofluorescence in the lesions inferiorly. The OS showed the presence of a healed macular lesion with RPE alterations and hypoautofluorescence on FAF imaging. There was an area of hyperautofluorescence at the superior arcade near the optic nerve head [Fig. 1].
OCT scans through the macula in OD showed a normal foveal contour with relative preservation of all the retinal layers. There were few hyperreflective foci in the inner retinal layers causing subtle back-shadowing on OCT. OCT scan through the macula of OS showed the presence of outer retinal disruption (disruption of the external limiting membrane [ELM], ellipsoid, and myoid zone) and mild RPE elevation and focal thickening [Fig. 2]. OCTA of OD showed an irregular decrease in the SCP and DCP. In addition, the choriocapillaris slab on automatic segmentation revealed few subtle hyporeflective areas suggestive of flow deficit. In OS, the OCTA at the level of SCP and DCP showed a more significant loss of vascular density compared to OD. The choriocapillaris slab in OS showed discrete areas of hyporeflectivity suggestive of flow deficit, more obvious compared to OD [Fig. 3].
The patient was followed up with no ocular treatment (oral hydroxychloroquine, started 6 weeks ago, was continued), and was afebrile and asymptomatic systemically at this time. Ten weeks after the episode of Chikungunya fever, he was systemically well, and BCVA measured 20/50 in OD and 20/40 in OS. There was no further improvement of BCVA or change in the fundus/OCTA appearance at 4-month follow-up visit.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 66-year-old Asian Indian male presented to the ophthalmology clinic with persistent bilateral decreased vision that began 15 days after an acute episode of febrile illness, severe arthralgia, and rash.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Six weeks prior to ophthalmic presentation, the patient developed high-grade fever with chills and rigors, severe arthralgia, papular skin rash, and fatigue, and was diagnosed with acute chikungunya fever (serum IgM positive). During the acute phase, he experienced severe fluid loss and acute renal failure requiring dialysis, and was treated with antipyretics, intravenous fluids, and oral hydroxychloroquine for arthritis. Fifteen days after fever onset, he developed bilateral decreased vision and photophobia, which was deferred for workup due to his systemic illness and persisted until his ophthalmology evaluation at 6 weeks post-onset.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recent acute chikungunya fever 6 weeks prior, complicated by acute kidney injury requiring transient dialysis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent bilateral decreased vision and prior photophobia, fever, chills, rigors, arthralgia, rash, and fatigue; afebrile and systemically asymptomatic at the 6-week ophthalmic visit. Current medication: oral hydroxychloroquine (started 6 weeks prior).

objective.physical_examination: Ophthalmological examination (6 weeks post-fever onset): best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) 20/60 in the right eye (OD) and 20/30 in the left eye (OS); no relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD); intraocular pressure 12 mm Hg OD and 13 mm Hg OS. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy: quiet anterior chamber with no inflammation, no vitritis, and a dense nuclear cataract in OD. Dilated fundus examination: OD showed peripapillary, inferior arcade, and temporal areas of depigmented healed retinitis lesions with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations sparing the macula; OS showed a healed macular lesion with RPE alterations.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial acute illness blood investigations: hemoglobin 13 g/dL, total leukocyte count 12,000/mm3, platelet count 150,000/mm3, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 34 mm/1st hour.
objective.advanced_workup: Fundus autofluorescence (FAF): OD showed stippled irregular hypoautofluorescence in nasal peripapillary lesions and hyperautofluorescence in inferior lesions; OS showed macular hypoautofluorescence and an area of hyperautofluorescence at the superior arcade near the optic disc. Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT): OD showed normal foveal contour with a few inner retinal hyperreflective foci causing subtle back-shadowing; OS showed outer retinal disruption (involving the external limiting membrane, ellipsoid zone, and myoid zone) with mild RPE elevation and focal thickening. OCT angiography (OCTA): bilateral irregular reduction in superficial and deep capillary plexus (SCP and DCP) vascular density and discrete hyporeflective choriocapillaris flow deficits, more pronounced in OS than OD.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Bilateral healed chikungunya retinitis with outer retinal disruption and retinal/choroidal microvascular ischemia (flow deficits). Confirmation: Positive serum chikungunya IgM during the preceding febrile episode coupled with characteristic multimodal retinal imaging (FAF, OCT, and OCTA) demonstrating healed retinitis and SCP/DCP/choriocapillaris flow deficits. Management and outcome: Observed conservatively without specific ocular therapy while continuing oral hydroxychloroquine for systemic arthritis. At 10 weeks post-illness, BCVA was 20/50 OD and 20/40 OS, remaining stable with unchanged fundus and OCTA findings at the 4-month follow-up.
